back: Signed 1959 (in force 1961) by 12 countries; reserves Antarctica for peace and science; territorial claims on hold.
Signed 1991 in Madrid (in force 1998): Antarctica a natural reserve; mining banned; EIA required for all activities.
Climate change, fishing (krill, toothfish), possible resource exploitation, tourism, pollution from stations and ships.

front: How does climate change affect Antarctica?
back: Warming on the Peninsula, ice-shelf collapse (e.g. Larsen B, 2002), sea-ice change affecting krill, melting land ice raising sea level.
The Commission for the Conservation of Antarctic Marine Living Resources sets catch limits for krill and toothfish and creates marine protected areas.
A study before an activity that predicts its environmental effects and decides whether and how it can go ahead.
Limit people ashore, keep distance from wildlife, clean boots and clothing, remove waste; voluntary and self-regulated.

front: Why does damage in Antarctica last a long time?
back: Cold slows decomposition and plant growth, so spills, waste and trampled moss recover only over decades.

front: Biggest limitation of the Antarctic Treaty system
back: It controls activities in Antarctica but cannot stop climate change caused by emissions elsewhere.
